subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public operator cron runs permanently record outcomes without owning any scheduler state, including counters, backoff, alerts, enabled state, one-shot consumption, and next-run timing?
rationale: The original destructive deletion is a bug, but extending non-consuming semantics across every scheduler-owned field is a broader compatibility policy that source correctness alone cannot authorize.

options.title: Accept non-consuming operators
options.body: Confirm the branch's explicit origin model so only timer and watcher-terminal runs may consume or mutate scheduler-owned state.

options.title: Narrow the behavior change
options.body: Limit the fix to one-shot deletion and separately design which counters, alerts, and timing fields manual runs should mutate.

options.title: Pause pending cron policy
options.body: Keep the PR open without landing until a different operator-versus-scheduler ownership contract is specified.

recommendation.title: Accept non-consuming operators
recommendation.body: Confirm the branch's explicit origin model so only timer and watcher-terminal runs may consume or mutate scheduler-owned state.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the strongest available routing candidate because their merged work established the adjacent on-exit consumption contract that the decision must preserve.
